name: Pralhad Joshi
role: Union Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and of New and Renewable Energy (2024–); additional charge of Education (from July 2026); Lok Sabha MP for Dharwad (2004–)
summary: Pralhad Joshi is a Bharatiya Janata Party member of the Lok Sabha for Dharwad and a Union minister. As Coal Minister he promoted coal output growth and commercial coal auctions, and as a minister he has defended the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, backed the abrogation of Article 370 and the school dress code during the 2022 Karnataka hijab row, and promoted the green hydrogen mission. His recorded statements on most of the test's topics are not on record, so most answers are null.

public-ownership.rationale: Joshi, as Coal Minister, launched and promoted the commercial coal mine auctions from 2020, which opened coal mining to private bidders. In November 2020 he said 40 of the 42 bidders were private companies and presented the revenue gain for states, which is a measure that moves coal extraction away from public ownership. The answer rests on this policy record alone.

cut-welfare.rationale: On 4 August 2026, in the Rajya Sabha, Joshi said there would be no reduction of food grains to any state or beneficiary under the National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026. He has also defended continuing free ration schemes. The answer rests on his opposition to cuts, not on the dependency reason given in the statement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Joshi, as New and Renewable Energy Minister, announced a Rs 100 crore government call for pilot projects under the National Green Hydrogen Mission in November 2025 and described the government's aim of making India a global green hydrogen hub. This is a state-led push on a strategic sector, and the answer rests on that policy alone.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: In September 2019 Joshi said three generations had waited for the abrogation of Article 370 and Article 35A, and in the Lok Sabha debate of August 2019 he backed the national parliament's removal of Jammu and Kashmir's special status. This supports Parliament withdrawing a region's special powers. The answer rests on the abrogation only.

notes: Living person: answers only from statements or measures he stated or drove; no party-based inference. Not answered despite partial evidence: restrict-conversion (he welcomed a law on conversion for marriage in late 2020, but the only page found was blocked to the fetch tool, so it is not cited); ban-cattle-slaughter (2019 remarks in Goa reported as undecided and dependent on public feeling; the more supportive quote appeared only in search snippets); drastic-climate-action (coal-to-2040 and renewables-push remarks found only in search snippets). Most of his record (Karnataka politics, caste survey, Dharmasthala, CAA defence, Lok Sabha speeches) is on party or communal matters that map to no statement here. Sources were news reports and state broadcaster copies; the Lok Sabha and PIB texts were not reachable.
